mainEntity.name: Can an attached in-law suite include a full kitchen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether a full kitchen is allowed depends on local municipal zoning classifications and your property's deed or HOA covenants. Many suburban jurisdictions permit a kitchenette containing a small sink, compact refrigerator, and countertop appliances, but restrict full 240-volt range hookups or full-sized ovens in attached additions to prevent unauthorized multi-family conversions. In some zoning districts, full accessory dwellings are permitted with specific parking and utility conditions. A contractor reviews municipal building codes and homeowner association rules to confirm what cooking appliances are legally permitted for your property.
acceptedAnswer.description: It depends on local zoning and HOA rules. Many areas permit kitchenettes with small sinks and refrigerators, but restrict full ranges in single-family residential zones.
